hook.situation: One day, four Korean tasks: answer an interview question, send a formal email, talk with coworkers, and reply to a friend on KakaoTalk. The grammar changes because the relationship changes.
objectives: Run a production checklist before sending or saying Korean.
Revise the same idea across interview, email, coworker talk, and friend chat.
Catch mismatches in particles, tense, honorifics, connectors, and style.
hook.whyItMatters: The final skill is not knowing more patterns. It is choosing the right Korean surface for the situation and then checking every layer before the sentence leaves your mouth or screen.

grammarNotes.title: Integrated production checklist
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Before producing Korean, ask: who is listening, what is the purpose, and what style does this channel require? Then check the grammar pieces.
grammarNotes.formation: Purpose -> listener -> channel -> style -> particles -> tense/aspect -> connectors -> closing.

examples.ko: 면접 답변은 정중하게 말하고, 경험의 시제를 흔들리지 않게 맞춰야 해요.
examples.romanization: myeonjeop dapbyeoneun jeongjunghage malhago, gyeongheomui sijereul heundeulliji anke matchwoya haeyo.
examples.en: For an interview answer, speak courteously and keep the tense of your experience consistent.
examples.note: Interview Korean checks register and tense together.

examples.ko: 공식 이메일에서는 확인 부탁드립니다처럼 마무리를 격식 있게 써야 해요.
examples.romanization: gongsik imeireseoneun hwagin butakdeurimnidacheoreom mamurireul gyeoksik itge sseoya haeyo.
examples.en: In a formal email, the closing should be formal, like 확인 부탁드립니다.
examples.note: Email Korean needs closing phrases, not only correct grammar.

examples.ko: 친구 카톡에서는 편하게 써도 되지만 회사 메일에는 ㅋㅋ를 빼야 해요.
examples.romanization: chingu katogeseoneun pyeonhage sseodo doejiman hoesa meileneun kkreul ppaeya haeyo.
examples.en: You can write casually in a friend's KakaoTalk chat, but you must remove ㅋㅋ from a company email.

exceptions: Do not treat the checklist as a fixed word order. It is a review habit.
If one layer changes, recheck the others. Formalizing a sentence can change endings, vocabulary, connectors, and closing.

grammarNotes.title: Rewrite by relationship, not by adding 요
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Politeness is a system. Adding 요 to slang or casual sentence shape does not make the whole sentence appropriate.
grammarNotes.formation: Casual idea -> polite neutral sentence -> formal written sentence.

examples.ko: 친구: ㅇㅇ 확인했어. / 회사 메일: 네, 확인했습니다.
examples.romanization: chingu: ngng hwaginhaesseo. / hoesa meil: ne, hwaginhaetseumnida.
examples.en: Friend: Yep, I checked. / Company email: Yes, I have confirmed it.
examples.note: ㅇㅇ changes to 네, and the ending changes to -했습니다.

examples.ko: 친구: 그 영상 개웃겨. / 면접: 그 사례가 매우 인상적이었습니다.
examples.romanization: chingu: geu yeongsang gaeutgyeo. / myeonjeop: geu saryega maeu insangjeogieotseumnida.
examples.en: Friend: That video is hilarious. / Interview: That example was very impressive.
examples.note: The rough slang is rewritten, not decorated.

examples.ko: 친구: 늦어서 미안. / 공식 이메일: 답장이 늦어져 죄송합니다.
examples.romanization: chingu: neujeoseo mian. / gongsik imeil: dapjangi neujeojyeo joesonghamnida.
examples.en: Friend: Sorry I'm late. / Formal email: I apologize for the delayed reply.
examples.note: Formal email uses a different phrase and a different sentence shape.

exceptions: 요 can make a sentence polite, but it cannot make rough slang formal.
Some friendly workplace chats allow softer language, but official emails still need complete phrases.

grammarNotes.title: The three quiet failure points
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Learners often notice vocabulary errors, but native readers feel particle, tense, and connector errors first because those pieces control the sentence relationship.
grammarNotes.formation: After the sentence sounds meaningful, check: noun role, event time, and sentence relationship.

examples.ko: 이 문장은 뜻은 맞지만 입자가 어색해요.
examples.romanization: i munjangeun tteuseun matjiman ipjaga eosaekaeyo.
examples.en: The meaning of this sentence is right, but the particle is awkward.

examples.ko: 경험을 말할 때는 과거 시제를 안정적으로 유지해야 해요.
examples.romanization: gyeongheomeul malhal ttaeneun gwageo sijereul anjeongjeogeuro yujihaeya haeyo.
examples.en: When talking about experience, you need to keep the past tense stable.
examples.note: Interview answers often talk about past experience.

examples.ko: 공식 글에서는 그래서보다 따라서가 더 자연스러울 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: gongsik geureseoneun geuraeseoboda ttaraseoga deo jayeonseureoul su isseoyo.
examples.en: In formal writing, 따라서 can be more natural than 그래서.
examples.note: Connector choice depends on register and logic.

exceptions: A short friend chat can omit pieces that a formal email cannot omit.
A connector is not decoration. It must match result, contrast, clarification, or summary.

grammarNotes.title: One idea, four Korean versions
grammarNotes.mentalModel: A strong learner can keep the same message while changing the surface for each situation.
grammarNotes.formation: Message idea: I checked it and will revise it. Change the style by channel.

examples.ko: 면접: 관련 경험을 검토했고, 필요한 부분을 개선하겠습니다.
examples.romanization: myeonjeop: gwallyeon gyeongheomeul geomtohaetgo, piryohan bubuneul gaeseonhagetseumnida.
examples.en: Interview: I have reviewed the related experience and will improve the necessary parts.

examples.ko: 이메일: 자료 확인 후 수정해서 다시 보내드리겠습니다.
examples.romanization: imeil: jaryo hwagin hu sujeonghaeseo dasi bonaedeurigetseumnida.
examples.en: Email: After checking the materials, I will revise them and send them again.

examples.ko: 동료 대화: 자료 확인했고, 필요한 부분은 다시 고칠게요.
examples.romanization: dongnyo daehwa: jaryo hwaginhaetgo, piryohan bubuneun dasi gochilgeyo.
examples.en: Coworker talk: I checked the materials, and I'll fix the necessary parts.

examples.ko: 친구 카톡: 봤어. 내가 다시 고칠게 ㅋㅋ.
examples.romanization: chingu katok: bwasseo. naega dasi gochilge kk.
examples.en: Friend KakaoTalk: Saw it. I'll fix it again lol.

exceptions: Do not use the friend version as the base for every context.
The safest production path is often to draft the formal version first, then relax it for casual settings.

exampleSentence.en: First, you need to decide the situation and listener.
exampleSentence.note: The first step in production review.

exampleSentence.en: The style changes depending on who the listener is.

exampleSentence.ko: 공식 이메일에서는 문체를 끝까지 격식 있게 맞춰야 해요.
exampleSentence.en: In a formal email, the style should stay formal until the end.
exampleSentence.note: Style consistency is the final chapter's main habit.

exampleSentence.en: Lastly, I will check even each particle again.

exampleSentence.ko: 면접 답변에서는 시제를 안정적으로 유지해야 해요.
exampleSentence.en: In an interview answer, you need to keep the tense stable.
exampleSentence.note: Experience answers often fail when tense shifts.

exampleSentence.ko: 이메일에서는 연결어와 마무리를 같이 확인해야 해요.
exampleSentence.en: In an email, you need to check the connectors and the closing together.
exampleSentence.note: Formal writing needs logical links and a closing.

exampleSentence.en: For an interview answer, you should check honorific language first.
exampleSentence.note: Respectful language belongs to relationship control.

exampleSentence.en: I apologize for the delayed reply.
In an interview, it is good to answer courteously.
exampleSentence.note: Useful register adjective for speech style.

extendedDialogue.setting: A learner reviews four Korean outputs from the same day.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 오늘 면접 답변, 이메일, 카톡 답장을 한 번에 검수해 볼까요?
lines.romanization: oneul myeonjeop dapbyeon, imeil, katok dapjangeul han beone geomsuhae bolkkayo?
lines.en: Shall we review today's interview answer, email, and KakaoTalk reply together?
lines.grammarNote: The final chapter reviews production across channels.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 먼저 상황과 상대방을 정하고 문체를 맞춰야 해요.
lines.romanization: meonjeo sanghwanggwa sangdaebangeul jeonghago munchereul matchwoya haeyo.
lines.en: First, decide the situation and listener, then match the style.
lines.grammarNote: 상황 and 상대방 come before grammar selection.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 면접 답변은 높임말과 시제를 확인하고, 이메일은 연결어와 마무리를 봐요.
lines.romanization: myeonjeop dapbyeoneun nopimmalgwa sijereul hwaginhago, imeireun yeongyeoreowa mamurireul bwayo.
lines.en: For the interview answer, check honorifics and tense; for the email, check connectors and the closing.
lines.grammarNote: Different channels require different review priorities.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 카톡에서는 편하게 써도 되지만 회사 메일에는 ㅋㅋ를 빼야 해요.
lines.romanization: katogeseoneun pyeonhage sseodo doejiman hoesa meileneun kkreul ppaeya haeyo.
lines.en: You can write casually in KakaoTalk, but in a company email you need to remove ㅋㅋ.
lines.grammarNote: Slang belongs to the relationship, not merely the app.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: Lastly, I will check even each particle again.

readingText.title: 하루 안에서 문체 바꾸기
readingText.body: 한국어를 잘 쓴다는 것은 단어를 많이 아는 것만으로 끝나지 않는다. 면접 답변에서는 정중한 문체와 안정적인 시제가 필요하고, 공식 이메일에서는 확인 부탁드립니다 같은 마무리 표현과 자연스러운 연결어가 필요하다. 반면에 친구 카톡에서는 짧고 편한 표현이 더 자연스러울 수 있다. 중요한 것은 같은 생각을 상황에 맞게 다시 쓰는 능력이다. 문장을 보내기 전에는 상대방, 목적, 문체, 입자, 시제, 연결어를 차례로 확인해야 한다.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Writing Korean well is not just knowing many words. An interview answer needs a courteous style and stable tense, while a formal email needs closing phrases such as 확인 부탁드립니다 and natural connectors. By contrast, short and relaxed expressions may be more natural in a friend's KakaoTalk chat. What matters is the ability to rewrite the same idea for the situation. Before sending a sentence, check the listener, purpose, style, particles, tense, and connectors in order.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 공식 이메일에서는 무엇을 확인해야 하나요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 마무리 표현과 자연스러운 연결어를 확인해야 합니다.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 문장을 보내기 전에 어떤 항목을 확인해야 하나요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 상대방, 목적, 문체, 입자, 시제, 연결어를 확인해야 합니다.

culturalNote.title: Advanced Korean is register control
culturalNote.body: A fluent Korean learner does not sound advanced because every sentence is long. They sound advanced because they know when to be brief, when to be warm, when to be formal, and when to remove slang completely. Register control is not extra polish; it is part of meaning.
culturalNote.tip: If you are unsure, make the sentence complete and neutral first. Then relax it only when the relationship clearly allows it.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence fits a formal company email?
inlineExercises.explanation: 부탁드립니다 is a formal written request ending.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which item should you decide before choosing slang or honorifics?
따라서와 ㅋㅋ가 한 문단에 같이 있으면 무엇이 문제인가요?
inlineExercises.explanation: Formal connectors and casual chat reactions usually do not belong in the same paragraph.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which review layer checks 은/는, 이/가, 을/를?
친구 카톡: 봤어. 내가 다시 고칠게 ㅋㅋ. What should change for a formal email?
options: 자료 확인 후 수정해서 다시 보내드리겠습니다.
inlineExercises.correct: 자료 확인 후 수정해서 다시 보내드리겠습니다.
inlineExercises.explanation: The formal email version rewrites the sentence, removes slang, and uses a formal ending.

bullets: The final review starts with purpose, listener, and channel before grammar.
Check 문체, 입자, 시제, 높임말, 연결어, and closing phrases together.
Adding 요 does not make slang formal; rewrite the whole sentence when the relationship changes.
A strong learner can express the same idea as an interview answer, formal email, coworker chat, and friend KakaoTalk reply.
